channel.title: The Daily Globe – Articles and Daily Briefings
channel.description: Headlines from around the world, updated every few minutes

item.title: The Bank of England has raised rates to 4%. What it means for your mortgage, savings and loans
item.description: Bank Rate went up by a quarter of a point on 5 November, the first rise since the cutting cycle began in 2024. We explain why, who feels it first, and what to watch before the next decision on 17 December.

item.title: The energy price cap explained: what £1,723 really means for your bills this winter
item.description: Ofgem's cap rose 4% on 1 October, while VAT on electricity was cut to zero. We explain what the cap limits, what it does not, why wholesale gas drives it, and what the Budget changed for 2027.

item.title: The Strait of Hormuz: why a war in the Gulf is pushing up UK prices
item.description: About a quarter of the world's seaborne oil trade passes through one narrow channel off Iran. We explain how disruption there feeds into petrol, energy bills, inflation and mortgage rates in Britain.

item.title: Budget 2026: the main changes for households, explained
item.description: Energy help, fuel duty, the minimum wage, tax on savings, help for first-time buyers and a new tax allowance for pensioners. A clear guide to what John Healey's 28 October Budget changes, and when.

item.title: The 2026 US midterms: how Congress elections work and what a Democratic Congress can and cannot do
item.description: Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate on 3 November. We explain how midterm elections work, when the new Congress takes over, and what powers it will have over President Trump's final two years.

item.title: UK inflation explained: what CPI, CPIH and "core" inflation actually measure
item.description: Inflation rose to 3.5% in September 2026, driven by petrol and diesel. Here is how the figure is calculated, why there are several measures, and how to read the next release on 18 November.

item.title: The state pension triple lock explained, and what "adjusting" it from 2030 could mean
item.description: The full new State Pension is £241.30 a week. We explain how the triple lock decides each year's rise, why it costs so much, the new Pension Tax Allowance from April 2027, and the open questions about the government's plan to change the lock.

item.title: UK GDP explained: what 0.7% growth tells us, and what a "recession" actually is
item.description: The economy grew 0.7% between July and September 2026, faster than expected despite the energy shock. We explain how GDP is measured, why first estimates get revised, and why "two quarters of decline" is only a rule of thumb.

item.title: Deficit, debt and "headroom": a plain-English guide to the UK's public finances
item.description: The government expects to borrow £133 billion this year and spend £124 billion on debt interest. We explain what the deficit and the national debt are, how the fiscal rules work, and why the war in the Middle East matters to the Treasury.

item.title: NATO's Article 5 explained: what "an attack on one is an attack on all" really commits countries to
item.description: Article 5 is the heart of the NATO alliance, but it does not automatically send troops to war. We explain the exact wording, how it is triggered, the one time it was used, and the new 5% defence spending pledge.

item.title: How the UN Security Council works, and why one veto can stop it
item.description: Fifteen members, five vetoes and the only UN body whose decisions every country must carry out. We explain how the Security Council votes, who sits on it now, and why it so often struggles to act on major wars.

item.title: How the WHO declares a global health emergency, and the new "pandemic emergency" alert
item.description: When an outbreak spreads, the World Health Organization can declare a "public health emergency of international concern". We explain who decides, what it changes, what it cannot do, and the higher alert level added after COVID-19.

item.title: How UK sanctions work: asset freezes, trade bans and who has to obey them
item.description: Sanctions are one of the main tools of UK foreign policy, from Russia to terrorism. We explain what they are, how people and companies end up on the list, what an asset freeze actually does, and what happens to those who break the rules.

item.title: How UK general elections work, and the changes coming: votes at 16 and bank cards as voter ID
item.description: 650 constituencies, one vote each and the winner takes the seat. We explain first past the post, who can vote, the five-year limit on a Parliament, the photo ID rules, and what the Representation of the People Bill would change.

item.title: How EU laws are made: a guide for UK readers
item.description: The UK left the EU, but EU rules still shape what British businesses sell into Europe's single market. We explain who proposes EU laws, how the Parliament and Council agree them, and the difference between a regulation and a directive.

item.title: How to Start an Online Shop in the UK in 2026: A Beginner's Guide
item.description: A plain-English UK guide to starting an online shop in 2026: HMRC and the £1,000 trading allowance, choosing products, Shopify vs Etsy vs WooCommerce, payments, shipping and marketing.

item.title: Daily World Briefing: Friday 30 October 2026
item.description: The main stories around the world as of Friday 30 October 2026, in our own words from UN News reporting: the Dnipro rail station strike, Sudan, Haiti's hunger crisis, Afghanistan's opium rebound, Myanmar and the vote on the Cuba embargo.

item.title: Ebola in DR Congo passes 10,000 cases: what we know
item.description: The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in DR Congo is the country's largest ever. We explain the numbers, the spread to Kenya and the vaccine trial that has just begun.

item.title: Three UN-backed climate reports in one week: what they say before COP31
item.description: Record heat deaths, record greenhouse gases and a weakening ocean carbon sink. A plain-English guide to three new reports released ahead of the COP31 climate conference in Antalya.
